reasoning: Both sets share the same scaffolding: a single rllab package, an interface task first, then spines, wiring and a system task, with frozen contract sections and samples. They differ most on RL substance and on how complete the builder packets are. Set A sets out a clear concept ladder for each stage: tabular Q-learning, then compact-view DQN, then full-grid CNN DQN with ablations of memory, target copy and exploration; REINFORCE then PPO on one fish, then a school, then limited sight; and fixed opponents, then naive co-learning, then pool self-play with cross-play ratings. It gives explicit rewards (SNAKE-06, FISH-05, HUNT-03/04), and its truncation-versus-termination handling is right for bootstrapping. Its Snake packet holds exact, board-level golden cases. Its weaknesses are stale framing and size. The brief still says 'Designing future environments now' is not being done, and its success section covers Snake only. The roadmap's S2 outline and ideas file talk about a 'deliberately revised shared core', but AD-09 and AD-13 build the batch-first, team-keyed core in M1, so CORE-06 becomes a near-vacuous check. Each stage is one large milestone. Set B has the better learner-facing brief and roadmap, a sensible walking-skeleton M1 (online Q-learning, thickened to DQN in M2), and hand-derived check worlds as a guard against silent bugs. But it never specifies a reward function for Snake, the fish or predator-prey anywhere in the spec, contract or tests. That is a real RL-soundness gap, and it leaves the Snake world task underspecified. SNAKE-07's 'moves right' contradicts the relative-turn action space. M3 ('Check and explain the snake') is a carved-off leftover of reference check plus write-up. M1 has no replay even though watching a replay is a core success criterion. The M1-T09 packet omits types it needs (core.Policy, WorldSpec, the train_loop signature). On balance A's content is stronger, and B's slightly better structure does not make up for it.

strengths: Explicit RL concept ladders per stage (tabular→DQN→CNN, REINFORCE→PPO→school→limited sight, fixed→co-learning→pool self-play)
Rewards, truncation vs termination and observation layouts fully specified
Ablations of memory, target copy and exploration teach why each piece matters
Snake packet carries exact board-level golden cases (TC-01–TC-10)
Reference mapping pins library defaults so a gap points at the learner's own code
weaknesses: Stale framing about a 'revised core' that M1 already builds
Brief's 'Not doing' and success sections still Snake-only
One very large milestone per stage instead of a walking skeleton first
Very dense docs for a solo learner

strengths: Clear learner-facing brief and roadmap outlines ('I can…')
M1 walking skeleton with thickening to full DQN in M2
Hand-derived check worlds gate every batch against silent RL bugs
Replay re-simulation via Trace with side-by-side checkpoints

A: M1-T06: train contract mixes in self-play/generation behaviour without saying which part the M1 spine must implement versus leave for M3
B: M1-T06: no reward values for Snake (food/death) anywhere in the packet or spec; Step.rewards cannot be filled
M1-T09: packet lacks the train_loop signature, core.Policy, WorldSpec/TeamSpec and NonFiniteError definitions it must use
M1-T15: SNAKE-07 rule says 'moves right', which can't map onto the relative straight/left/right action space without an interpretation the packet doesn't give
